content: The Barbarian class has a hit die of 12 and proficiency choices in Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, and Survival. Proficiencies include Light Armor, Medium Armor, Shields, Simple Weapons, Martial Weapons, and saving throws for STR and CON. Starting equipment consists of an Explorer's Pack and 4 javelins, with options for a greataxe or any martial melee weapon, and two handaxes or any simple weapon. Multi-classing prerequisites require a minimum STR score of 13, along with proficiency in Shields, Simple Weapons, and Martial Weapons. The subclass available is the Berserker.

name: Bard

proficiency_choices.desc: Three musical instruments of your choice

starting_equipment_options.desc: (a) a rapier, (b) a longsword, or (c) any simple weapon
(a) a diplomat’s pack or (b) an entertainer’s pack
(a) a lute or (b) any other musical instrument

info.name: Cantrips
desc: You know two cantrips of your choice from the bard spell list. You learn additional bard cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Bard table.

info.name: Spell Slots
desc: The Bard table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
For example, if you know the 1st-level spell cure wounds and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast cure wounds using either slot.

info.name: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher
desc: You know four 1st-level spells of your choice from the bard spell list.
The Spells Known column of the Bard table shows when you learn more bard spells of your choice.
Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown on the table. For instance, when you reach 3rd level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the bard spells you know and replace it with another spell from the bard spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

info.name: Spellcasting Ability
desc: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your bard spells. Your magic comes from the heart and soul you pour into the performance of your music or oration. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a bard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

info.name: Ritual Casting
desc: You can cast any bard spell you know as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag.

info.name: Spellcasting Focus
desc: You can use a musical instrument (see Equipment) as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells.

content: The Bard class has a hit die of 8 and proficiency choices for skills like Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Arcana, and more. Proficiencies include Light Armor, Simple Weapons, and saving throws for DEX and CHA. Starting equipment includes Leather Armor and a Dagger, with options for a Rapier, Longsword, or simple weapon. The Bard can cast spells using CHA as their spellcasting ability, with abilities like Cantrips, Spell Slots, and Ritual Casting. Musical instruments like the Lute can be used as a spellcasting focus. The Lore subclass is available, and multi-classing requires a minimum CHA score of 13.

(a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
(a) a priest’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack

info.name: Cantrips
desc: At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the cleric spell list. You learn additional cleric cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Cleric table.

info.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
desc: The Cleric table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of cleric spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the cleric spell list. When you do so, choose a number of cleric spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your cleric level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

For example, if you are a 3rd-level cleric, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With a Wisdom of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination. If you prepare the 1st-level spell cure wounds, you can cast it using a 1st-level or 2nd-level slot. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of cleric spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

info.name: Spellcasting Ability
desc: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your cleric spells. The power of your spells comes from your devotion to your deity. You use your Wisdom whenever a cleric spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a cleric spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

info.name: Ritual Casting
desc: You can cast a cleric spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

info.name: Spellcasting Focus
desc: You can use a holy symbol (see Equipment) as a spellcasting focus for your cleric spells.

content: The Cleric class is a versatile spellcaster with a hit die of 8, proficient in light armor, medium armor, shields, simple weapons, and saving throws for Wisdom and Charisma. They can choose two skills from History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion, making them adept at knowledge and social interactions. Starting with a shield and the option for a mace or warhammer, scale mail, leather armor, chain mail, a light crossbow with bolts, and a priest's or explorer's pack, the Cleric is well-equipped for various situations. With a focus on Wisdom, they excel in spellcasting, preparing cleric spells equal to their Wisdom modifier + cleric level, using a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus. The Life subclass enhances their healing abilities, while multi-classing requires proficiency in light armor, medium armor, and shields, along with a minimum Wisdom score of 13. Ritual casting and a ritual spell can be performed if prepared, showcasing the Cleric's spiritual connection and devotion to their deity.

content: The Paladin class has a hit die of 10 and proficiency choices that include skills like Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion, as well as proficiencies in all armor, shields, simple weapons, martial weapons, and saving throws for Wisdom and Charisma. Starting equipment includes Chain Mail and options for martial weapons, shields, javelins, and packs. Multi-classing prerequisites require a minimum Strength and Charisma score of 13 and grant proficiencies in light and medium armor, shields, simple weapons, and martial weapons. The subclass Devotion is available, and spellcasting at level 2 is based on Charisma, allowing preparation and casting of spells from the paladin spell list. Charisma is also the spellcasting ability for setting DC and attack rolls, with a holy symbol as the spellcasting focus.

content: The Ranger class has a hit die of 10 and proficiency choices in Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival. Proficiencies include Light Armor, Medium Armor, Shields, Simple Weapons, Martial Weapons, and saving throws for DEX and STR. Proficient in light armor, simple weapons, longswords, rapiers, shortswords, hand crossbows, and thieves' tools, Rogues also have saving throws for Dexterity and Intelligence. Starting equipment includes leather armor, daggers, and thieves' tools, with options for a rapier or shortsword, a shortbow with arrows or a shortsword, and various packs. Multi-classing requires a minimum Dexterity score of 13 and grants similar proficiencies and skill choices. The Thief subclass further enhances Rogue abilities, making them agile and resourceful in any situation.

content: The Wizard class has a hit die of 6 and proficiency choices for Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, and Religion. content: The Druid class in Dungeons & Dragons has a hit die of 8 and specializes in nature-based magic. Proficiency choices include skills like Arcana, Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion, and Survival, with options for light and medium armor, shields, and various weapons. Saving throws are based on Intelligence and Wisdom. Starting equipment includes leather armor and an Explorer's Pack, along with a choice of a wooden shield or simple weapon.
